newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks down led by banks, manufacturing.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks down led by banks, manufacturing.

text.p: Colombian stocks were led slightly lower by banks and manufacturing in a sluggish session, brokers said Wednesday.
Bogota's IBB index dropped 0.23 percent to 1,070.12 amid a 2.4 billion peso volume while Medellin's IBOMED general price index fell 0.17 percent to 16,566.45 amid a 1.9 billion peso volume.

"Whichever way you look at it, this market is speculative. When prices drop, everybody moves to sell and when there's gains, everybody starts to buy. The trend at the moment is downward because investors are reshuffling portfolios," a Bogota broker said.
Brewing giant Bavaria fell 1.14 percent to 6,900 in Bogota and 1.43 percent to the same price in Medellin.

Banco de Bogota fell 1.58 percent to 6,200 in Bogota and was not traded in Medellin. Banco de Colombia continued to fall, closing down 0.23 percent at 423 in Bogota and 0.21 percent to 422.1 in Medellin.

Greater falls in the index were once again offset by gains in insurance company Suramericana de Seguros, part of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno group. It rose 0.43 percent to 23,100 in both Bogota and Medellin.
